import torch, torch.nn as nn, __main__, hashlib
from collections import deque
class Maze(nn.Module): pass
__main__.Maze = Maze
m = torch.load('maze.pt', map_location='cpu', weights_only=False)
g = m.maze.weight.data.int().tolist()
R=len(g); C=len(g[0])
start=end=None
for i in range(R):
    for j in range(C):
        if g[i][j]==2: start=(i,j)
        if g[i][j]==3: end=(i,j)
print('start',start,'end',end)
# BFS
from collections import deque
def neighbors(p):
    i,j=p
    return [((i-1,j),'W'),((i+1,j),'S'),((i,j-1),'A'),((i,j+1),'D')]
dist={start:0}
prev={start:None}
q=deque([start])
while q:
    p=q.popleft()
    if p==end: break
    for (np,mv) in neighbors(p):
        i,j=np
        if 0<=i<R and 0<=j<C and g[i][j]!=1 and np not in dist:
            dist[np]=dist[p]+1
            prev[np]=(p,mv)
            q.append(np)
print('dist to end', dist.get(end))
# reconstruct
path=[]
p=end
while prev[p] is not None:
    pp,mv=prev[p]
    path.append(mv)
    p=pp
path=path[::-1]
s=''.join(path)
print('path len',len(s))
print(s)
print('md5', hashlib.md5(s.encode()).hexdigest())
EOF"}
